info.title: SMSOne Enterprise API
info.description:
Enterprise Spring Modulith template API. Every response uses the unified envelope ({data | errors, meta, links}) with meta.requestId always present; quote the requestId when reporting issues.

Operations are grouped as `<axis> · <resource>`. The axis is the authority the operation enforces — Platform (a realm role), Organization (a permission inside one tenant), Shared (any authenticated caller) — and it is read from the code that enforces it, so a group name cannot promise access the API will refuse.

servers.description: Local, direct to the service (bypasses the gateway)

tags.name: Platform · Users & impersonation
tags.description: Identities across every tenant, and the impersonation sessions that are the only sanctioned way from an operator to tenant data. platform-support reads and may open a session; wearing an account that itself holds a platform role needs platform-superadmin. A session carries no authority of its own, so from inside one this whole group answers 403.

tags.name: Platform · Organizations
tags.description: Creating a tenant, suspending it, reactivating it. These are platform actions ON an organization, not actions inside one, and that is why they are here: a fresh org has no member to hold a permission, and suspension cuts every member's access — neither can be gated on a permission granted inside the org being acted on. Reading and editing the record itself is the tenant's own business: Organization · Profile.

tags.name: Platform · Settings & flags
tags.description: Writing platform-wide configuration: setting values and feature-flag state, platform-admin. The same keys are readable by any authenticated caller under Shared · Settings & flags — same paths, different method, different authority, which is why one controller lands in two groups.

tags.name: Platform · Support queue
tags.description: The cross-tenant support queue (platform-support): work tickets, assign, reply (public or an internal note the tenant never sees), transition status. SLA breaches escalate automatically — a minute job bumps priority, counts the breach, and fires org.ticket.escalated.

tags.name: Platform · SLA policies
tags.description: Per-org SLA overrides (platform-admin writes, platform-support reads): set an org's first-response/resolution targets tighter or looser than the seeded per-priority defaults. Consulted at ticket open.

tags.name: Platform · Retention
tags.description: Per-org retention overrides (platform-admin writes, platform-support reads) for the org-scoped logs (webhook-delivery, exchange-job): keep or drop one org's rows on a different schedule than the platform default.

tags.name: Platform · Maintenance
tags.description: Scheduling maintenance windows (platform-admin), platform-wide or targeted at one org. RESTRICT pauses org writes for the window; ANNOUNCE is banner-only. Distinct from a tenant's lifecycle (Platform · Organizations) — those are permanent, these are time-boxed.

tags.name: Platform · Compliance
tags.description: Legal holds and erasure execution. A hold (subject or org) BLOCKS the retention purge and any erasure of the held data until released — placing is platform-admin, listing platform-support. Erasure soft-deletes now, hard-erases at retention (which honors holds).

tags.name: Platform · Integrations
tags.description: The PLATFORM-DEFAULT provider configs (platform-admin) — SMS, email, payment gateway — used by any org that has no override of its own. Same encryption and masking as the org surface.

tags.name: Platform · API keys
tags.description: Platform machine credentials — support-tier keys minted by platform-admin. They read platform surfaces; they never satisfy a higher tier or carry org permissions.

tags.name: Platform · Billing & plans
tags.description: The commercial axis of a tenant: the seeded plan catalogue and each org's subscription. Reading is platform-support; assigning a plan is platform-admin, audited, and bites the very next entitlement gate. A tenant reads its own state under Organization · Profile's surface.

tags.name: Platform · Ops
tags.description: Running the platform: scheduler lock state (proof that clustered jobs fire once), the curated analytics reports, and the cross-tenant audit trail. Read-only and platform-support throughout — investigating is the support job. One tenant's own view of that trail is Organization · Audit.

tags.name: Organization · Profile
tags.description: The organization record as its own members see it: read on org:read, edit on org:update. Lifecycle is deliberately absent — that is Platform · Organizations.

tags.name: Organization · Members
tags.description: Who belongs to one tenant and as what: list, invite, re-role, remove. Handing someone a role IS granting its permissions, so invite and re-role are additionally refused when they would grant more than the caller holds.

tags.name: Organization · Groups
tags.description: Named funnels that confer one role to their members, unioned with each member's own — the resolver adds the group's permissions, never replaces them. Managing a group is member:role:assign (a group can't grant more than its creator holds); reading is member:read. A group extends a member, it is not a way in.

tags.name: Organization · Roles
tags.description: A tenant's roles — named bundles of permission codes from the fixed catalogue (Shared · Reference data). Role codes are inert: no request path resolves authority from a code, only from the permission set. System roles refuse edits.

tags.name: Organization · Webhooks
tags.description: One tenant's outbound event subscriptions and their delivery attempts, all on webhook:manage. Endpoint URLs are SSRF-checked before they are stored, and every delivery is signed and retried with backoff before it dead-letters.

tags.name: Organization · Audit
tags.description: The audit trail scoped to one tenant, on audit:read — an org's own admins can review their trail without any platform access. Rows written during an impersonation session name the operator, not the account they wore.

tags.name: Organization · Exchange
tags.description: Import and export as background jobs inside one tenant: submit answers 202 and the work is polled, never awaited. Submitting is additionally refused without the chosen handler's own permission — the handler is picked at runtime, so no annotation can name that gate. Job metadata reads on org:read; the artifacts (source, error report, result) answer only to the requester or a holder of that same handler permission. The handler catalogue itself is Shared · Exchange catalog.

tags.name: Organization · API keys
tags.description: An organization's machine credentials (apikey:manage). A key carries a SUBSET of its creator's permissions — it can never out-rank them — and authenticates as X-Api-Key. The secret shows once, at mint.

tags.name: Organization · Support
tags.description: The tenant's support tickets — open, read, reply (org:read). Internal platform notes are never shown here; escalation and assignment are the platform's job (Platform · Support queue). A public reply notifies the opener in-app.

tags.name: Organization · Maintenance
tags.description: The maintenance windows in effect for this tenant (platform-wide plus its own), read on org:read for a client banner. During a RESTRICT window this org's writes answer 503 + Retry-After; reads pass. Scheduling is Platform · Maintenance.

tags.name: Organization · Integrations
tags.description: The organization's provider overrides (org:update) — SMS, email, payment gateway. An override wins over the platform default for that capability. Secret values are encrypted at rest and masked on read; the platform defaults are Platform · Integrations.

tags.name: Organization · Security policy
tags.description: The organization's security policy (org:update to set, org:read to view): IP allowlist, require-a-trusted-device, session max age. Every field TIGHTENS access over the open default; a denial is a 403 naming the rule, distinct from RBAC. Blessing a member's device as trusted lives here too — trust is the org's grant, not a self-claim.

tags.name: Organization · Billing
tags.description: The tenant's own money view — invoices, proxied from Kill Bill on org:read. Plans, balances and billing actions are the platform's surface: Platform · Billing & plans.

tags.name: Organization · Exchange schedules
tags.description: Recurring exports on a cron (UTC), firing as their creator — whose export permission is re-checked at every fire, so a revocation stops the schedule loudly instead of letting it keep exporting. One-off jobs and their artifacts are Organization · Exchange.

tags.name: Shared · Me & notifications
tags.description: The caller's own identity and in-app notifications; no axis owns them because a tenant member and a platform operator both legitimately arrive here. GET /me is the one path the provisioning gate lets through for an un-provisioned subject (onboarding), and still a hard stop for a disabled one.

tags.name: Shared · Files
tags.description: Upload, download, delete, presign. The one group whose rule lives in the handler rather than in an annotation, which is exactly why neither axis claims it: your own namespace always, someone else's only with a platform tier (support to read, admin to delete).

tags.name: Shared · Settings & flags
tags.description: Reading platform configuration — settings and feature-flag state are visible to any authenticated caller, because how the application behaves is not a secret. Writing them is Platform · Settings & flags.

tags.name: Shared · Reference data
tags.description: Fixed vocabularies any authenticated caller may read — today the permission catalogue that Organization · Roles is composed from. A new shared read lands here until it earns a group of its own.

tags.name: Shared · Exchange catalog
tags.description: The exchange handler catalogue and its downloadable templates — which datasets can move, what each file must look like, which permissions gate it. Readable by any authenticated caller; running one is Organization · Exchange.

tags.name: Shared · My profile
tags.description: The caller's own record — profile, contacts, preferences, avatar, linked identity providers. No axis owns it: every row answers about YOU, whichever axis you arrived from. Support's read-only view of a user's profile is Platform · Users & impersonation.

tags.name: Shared · My devices
tags.description: The caller's own devices — register (idempotent per X-Device-Id), list, revoke. Marking one TRUSTED is not here: trust is an organization's grant (its security policy), not a self-claim.

tags.name: Shared · My privacy
tags.description: Your own compliance controls — consent history (append-only), a data export of your record (portability), and requesting your own erasure (GDPR art. 17; deferred while a legal hold is in force).

tags.name: Shared · Webhook events
tags.description: The subscribable webhook event vocabulary — the codes the subscription endpoints' events array accepts, with what each means. Managing subscriptions is Organization · Webhooks.
